comment: The operator-value half of Aerie's cluster configuration (the cluster plan Phase 3b.1).
Flux reconciles from git, and docs/ethos.md keeps operator values out of git - so the values
arrive out of band as one ConfigMap, and every Kustomization under deploy/ reaches them with
postBuild.substituteFrom. This file is the pointer half: it names each key, says where its
value comes from at provisioning time, and describes what a valid one looks like. It holds no
values, and it is structural - identical for every installation, which is why it is committed.
Consumed by scripts/k3s/Set-ClusterConfig.ps1 (renders and applies the ConfigMap) and by the
${...} substitutions in deploy/. Both halves must agree on these names, so change them here
and nowhere else. Same split, and the same reasoning, as scripts/secrets/parameters.json; the
difference is only sensitivity. Nothing here is secret, so it is applied in the clear and
printed in full in the run log, which is what makes an audit record of it worth having.
Fields:
key          - the ConfigMap key, and therefore the ${...} token manifests substitute.
SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE because Flux's postBuild is a shell-style expansion.
env          - environment variable Set-ClusterConfig.ps1 reads the value from. Equal to
'key' for every entry today, and kept as its own field anyway: a future key
that collides with something a CLI already owns - the way AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
does in parameters.json - has to be able to move without renaming the
substitution token every manifest uses.
githubSource - the repository variable provision-4-cluster-config.yml maps into 'env'.
githubKind   - always 'variable' here, and that is the point: an operator value is not a
secret, so it stays unmasked and legible in run logs. Note that reading one
through ${{ secrets.X }} resolves to an empty string rather than erroring.
required     - a run fails preflight if a required value is missing.
pattern      - .NET regex every value is checked against before anything is applied, and
checked case-SENSITIVELY, which PowerShell's -match is not. A typo'd hosted
zone id, a domain with a stray scheme on it, or a replica count of 30 is
otherwise diagnosed several steps later and reads as an AWS, cert-manager or
Longhorn failure rather than as the transcription error it is.
normalize    - optional; 'lower' folds the value before it is checked. Only for values whose
case genuinely carries no meaning - a domain name is case-insensitive by RFC,
so Example.com is a correct answer that Kubernetes would nonetheless reject as
an Ingress host, and folding it is better than refusing it. A hosted zone id
is the opposite: an opaque, case-sensitive string, where folding would invent
a zone that does not exist. When in doubt, leave it out and reject instead.
hint         - appended to the failure message when 'pattern' rejects a value.
example      - a syntactically valid value. Deliberately not this installation's.
consumedBy   - the the cluster plan step that first substitutes it.
description  - what it is and where the operator got it.

keys.hint: Just the base domain - no scheme, no trailing dot, no wildcard. Case is folded for you. The wildcard is added where it is needed (dnsNames becomes *.${DOMAIN} plus ${DOMAIN}, since a wildcard does not match the apex).
keys.consumedBy: 3b.10 wildcard Certificate; every Phase 5 Ingress host
keys.description: Base domain the cluster serves. Already supplied to cd.yml as vars.DOMAIN today.

keys.hint: One address, unwrapped - not a Name <addr> pair.
keys.description: Let's Encrypt account address. Expiry notices and account recovery go here.

keys.hint: A region id, not an availability zone or a display name - us-east-1, not us-east-1a and not 'US East'.
keys.description: Region holding the /aerie SSM parameter tree. Must be the same region Provision 2 seeded into - the tree lives in exactly one, and ESO reads it by region.

keys.hint: A bare IPv4 address, with no prefix length. It must sit on the nodes' own subnet - kube-vip answers ARP for it there - and outside the DHCP pool, with no reservation of its own: the VIP has no fixed MAC, which is the whole point of it.
keys.description: Floating ingress address, chosen and verified free in Phase 3a.2. Phase 7 is what finally points pfSense Unbound at it.

keys.hint: The interface name alone - eth0, not 2: eth0 and not eth0@if2. Read it with the command in Phase 3a.3.
keys.description: Interface kube-vip advertises the VIP on in ARP mode. Identical on every node, since they are built from one golden image - if it is not, Phase 3a.3 says stop and find out why.

keys.hint: The id only, uppercase - Z0123456789ABCDEFGHIJ. The console and the API both also render it as /hostedzone/Z..., and pasting that whole path is the usual mistake; strip the prefix.
keys.description: Public hosted zone for DOMAIN, from Phase 3a.4. Naming it explicitly stops cert-manager from having to enumerate zones, which the aerie-eso and Route53 policies are not scoped for.

keys.hint: Never more than the number of nodes that exist. A volume with more replicas than nodes is permanently Degraded, and its alarms are the noise that trains an operator to ignore the real ones.
keys.description: 2 during the two-node build window; Phase 7 raises it to 3 by changing this variable and re-running Provision 4 - no commit, which is the reason this is a ConfigMap and not a manifest.

keys.hint: Never more than the number of nodes that exist - required anti-affinity leaves the excess pod permanently Pending. Same shape and the same reasoning as LONGHORN_REPLICA_COUNT.
keys.description: 2 during the two-node build window; Phase 7 raises it to 3 alongside LONGHORN_REPLICA_COUNT by changing this variable and re-running Provision 4 - no commit.

keys.hint: Never more than the number of nodes that exist - required anti-affinity leaves the excess pod permanently Pending. Raising this above 1 also means adding a synchronous replication block to the Cluster, which is deliberately absent at one instance; the manifest says so where it matters.
keys.description: Instances in the Immich photo library's own Postgres cluster - not aerie-pg, which POSTGRES_INSTANCES sizes. Optional, and the manifest carries a ':=1' default, because Immich is not on the HA list: its recovery story is the offsite archive, and a standby would double the local-path footprint to protect data that already has WAL archiving and a nightly dump. Set it only if that judgement changes.

keys.hint: A valid S3 bucket name: lowercase, 3-63 characters, no underscores, no consecutive dots, not formatted as an IP address. The dedicated bucket from Phase 4a.2 - not the restic backup bucket.
keys.description: S3 bucket CloudNativePG's Barman Cloud Plugin archives WAL and base backups to. Per-installation, so it stays out of git per docs/ethos.md.

keys.hint: The HTTPS clone URL of the private per-installation site repo (Phase 5a.3) - no trailing .git, no credentials embedded in it. The credential is aerie-site-git, synced by 5b.1.
keys.description: Where image automation (5b.12) commits its tag bumps. Per-installation, so it stays out of git per docs/ethos.md.

keys.hint: Registry host plus namespace only - no image name, no tag, no trailing slash. ghcr.io/<owner>, not ghcr.io/<owner>/aerie-api:latest.
keys.description: Registry and namespace the api and kiosk-files images are pulled from. Keeps the owner out of git per docs/ethos.md.

keys.hint: A hostname or a bare IPv4 address - never a UNC path (no leading \\ or /) and never the bare NetBIOS name. The mount is performed by a resolver with no DNS suffix search list, no NetBIOS and no mDNS.
keys.description: FQDN or IP of the SMB server behind csi-driver-smb's mounts.

keys.hint: The share name alone, no slashes - not //host/share and not a path under the share.
keys.description: Split from SHARE_HOST because csi-driver-smb's source wants //host/share while the PV's volumeHandle also needs the host on its own.

keys.hint: A relative path under the share, no leading slash and no '..' segment. Unset turns media serving off entirely, exactly as today - it must not collapse to the share root.
keys.description: Subpath of the share served, unauthenticated, as the media library. Optional, and unset means off rather than root: an accidental empty value would otherwise publish the whole house share to anyone on the LAN, so the safe reading of 'no value' is 'serve nothing'.

keys.hint: One of none, canary, full. Unset means none - the pre-auth posture, which is also the rollback. Not off/on: those are YAML 1.1 booleans, and this value is substituted into a manifest that gets re-parsed, so a boolean word arrives as a boolean no matter how it is quoted.
keys.consumedBy: 5b.10 HelmRelease values (auth.mode), which sets api env Auth__Enabled/Auth__EnforceInProcess and decides which Ingresses carry the forwardAuth annotation
keys.description: How much of the house sits behind the wall (docs/plans/auth.md). 'none' is the pre-auth behavior and the complete rollback; 'canary' walls apps/docs alone with Traefik as the only enforcer; 'full' walls home and kiosk and the pod refuses on its own as well. One value, one ladder - moving between them is a repository-variable change and a reconcile, not a code change. The vocabulary avoids off/on on purpose: this value is substituted textually into a manifest that is then parsed as YAML 1.1, where those words are booleans regardless of quoting.

keys.hint: An IANA zone id in Area/Location form - America/New_York, not EST and not an offset.
keys.description: Already a cd.yml variable today; carried across unchanged.

keys.hint: A hostname or a bare IPv4 address for the Home Assistant instance.
keys.consumedBy: 5b.5 api env, once, on a fresh install's SiteSettings import; 6b.13 kuma-provision CronJob, every reconcile, forever
keys.description: Home Assistant host. Used to read only on a fresh install - a restore already has it in the database - but Phase 6's kuma-provision CronJob reads it on every run, which is why it is required from Phase 6 on rather than staying optional.

keys.hint: A TCP port, 1-65535.
keys.consumedBy: 5b.5 api env, once, on a fresh install's SiteSettings import; 6b.13 kuma-provision CronJob, every reconcile, forever
keys.description: Home Assistant port, same used-to-be-fresh-install-only caveat as HA_HOST - required from Phase 6 on because kuma-provision reads it every run.

keys.hint: A bracketed, comma-separated list of double-quoted host:port strings, and nothing else - no spaces, no trailing comma, no bare (unquoted) entries. The three Windows hosts' LAN addresses reserved in 6a.2, each with windows_exporter's port.
keys.description: The three physical Windows hosts' LAN addresses and windows_exporter's port, as one Prometheus-shaped list. Reserved as fixed addresses in 6a.2 - a lease change here is a firing up == 0, not a rediscovered host.

keys.hint: A bracketed, comma-separated list of double-quoted bare IPv4 addresses - no ports, no hostnames. kube-prometheus-stack's kubeEtcd.endpoints template emits one Endpoints subset address per entry and takes the port from kubeEtcd.service.port (2381) separately, so unlike WINDOWS_EXPORTER_TARGETS there is no :port suffix here.
keys.description: LAN addresses of every k3s **server** node (every node running --cluster-init/--server, i.e. every etcd member) - the same nodes 6b.1's etcd-expose-metrics config.yaml change was rolled out to. k3s's embedded etcd is not a pod, so there is no label to select it by the way kube-state-metrics selects everything else here; the chart's kubeEtcd.endpoints wants literal IPs instead, the same shape WINDOWS_EXPORTER_TARGETS already established for a hand-fed static target list. 2 during the two-node build window; Phase 7 adds the third server's address by changing this variable and re-running Provision 4 - no commit, same shape as LONGHORN_REPLICA_COUNT.

keys.hint: The webhook id alone - the trailing segment of the /api/webhook/<id> URL Home Assistant gave you when the automation was created in 6a.3. No slashes, and no leading /api/webhook/.
keys.description: Webhook id for the Home Assistant automation 6a.3 creates. Alertmanager posts to http://${HA_HOST}:${HA_PORT}/api/webhook/${HA_ALERT_WEBHOOK_ID}. An opaque per-installation string, and a repository variable rather than a secret: see 6a.3 for why.

keys.hint: The user or organization alone - the first path segment of the repository URL, with no slash and no repository name after it. Deliberately not named GITHUB_OWNER: GitHub refuses to store a repository variable whose name starts with GITHUB_.
keys.consumedBy: docs/plans/deploy-observability.md 1.2, the Delivery dashboard's GitHub panels
keys.description: Owner of the *Aerie* repository - the one CI runs in. Not the site repo, which SITE_REPO_URL already names, and not derivable from it: an installation may keep the two under different owners. Optional, and the manifest that reads it carries a `:=` empty default, so an installation that never sets it gets a Delivery dashboard whose CI row is empty rather than a Kustomization that fails strict substitution. Set it and the CI row fills in on the next reconcile - no commit.

keys.hint: The repository name alone - the second path segment, with no owner prefix and no .git suffix.
keys.consumedBy: docs/plans/deploy-observability.md 1.2, the Delivery dashboard's GitHub panels
keys.description: Name of the Aerie repository, paired with AERIE_REPO_OWNER. Two keys rather than one owner/name string because the grafana-github-datasource query model takes `owner` and `repository` as separate fields and Flux's substitution cannot split one value across two.

keys.hint: A restic repository string, not a bucket name and not an s3:// URL: the scheme is 's3:' with a colon and no slashes, the host is the bucket's REGIONAL endpoint, and there is no trailing slash. A prefix under the bucket is accepted and rarely wanted - Phase 0's repository sits at the bucket root.
keys.description: Off-site restic repository, created in Phase 0 and supplied to compose.backup.yml as a cd.yml variable until 7b.9 deleted both. The region lives inside the endpoint hostname on purpose: restic will not take it separately, so there is no RESTIC_AWS_REGION beside this key - one value that cannot disagree with itself beats two that can. Not WAL_BUCKET and not LONGHORN_BACKUP_BUCKET; three repositories, three buckets, three blast radii.

keys.hint: A relative path under the share, no leading slash and no '..' segment - the same shape MEDIA_LIBRARY_SUBPATH takes. Forward slashes if it is nested: it is joined into an SMB source of the form //host/share/subpath.
keys.description: Directory on the house share holding the local half of the restic repository pair - the copy 8a.2 moved off the old server, which keeps the name it had there rather than being shortened. Required where MEDIA_LIBRARY_SUBPATH is optional, and for the mirror image of that key's reasoning: an unset media subpath serves nothing, while an unset backup subpath would make the entire house share the restic repository.

keys.hint: A valid S3 bucket name: lowercase, 3-63 characters, no underscores, no consecutive dots, not formatted as an IP address. The name alone - Longhorn's own s3://bucket@region/ target is assembled in the manifest, so do not paste one here. The dedicated bucket Provision 6 created, and neither the WAL bucket nor the restic one.
keys.description: S3 bucket Longhorn writes volume backups into, from Phase 8a.1. A bucket name rather than the full s3://bucket@region/ string Longhorn wants, because AWS_REGION is already a key and a second copy of the region is a second thing that can be wrong - 8b.9 joins the two. Dedicated for the reason objectstore.yaml gives for the WAL bucket: Longhorn owns the backupstore/ layout underneath it and expects to be its only writer.
